answer: A river survey splits a fixed reward pool by grid cells sampled each hour, whether stations track yarrow or timber drift. An inspector signs the cell, hour, reading and station key after a spot check; the ledger counts each cell and hour once. Extra aliases in one cell add no weight, even if they collude. To gain weight, a farm must install and service stations in more cells. This assumes honest inspectors and a grid fixed before claims open. A newcomer can cover one unserved cell with a loaned sensor.
